comparisons.peer_summary: Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM) consists of two primary businesses: Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank, with Merrill focused on clients with over $250,000 in assets and both units serving high net worth clients.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America structure their wealth management operations into distinct private bank and mass-affluent segments. Citi reports $402 billion in USPB and Wealth deposits and emphasizes long-term client tenure (e.g., 66% of Citigold clients >10 years). Bank of America defines its Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM) segment similarly with Merrill Wealth Management (>$250k assets) and Bank of America Private Bank, but its disclosure focuses on business composition and advisor networks rather than aggregate deposit balances or retention tenure in this specific text.

sentences.text: Citi also has a strong consumer and wealth deposit base, with $402 billion of USPB and Wealth deposits as of year end, which are diversified across the Private Bank, Citigold and Wealth at Work within Wealth, as well as USPB, and across regions and products.

As of year end, approximately 66% of U.S. Citigold clients have been with Citi for more than 10 years and approximately 39% of Private Bank ultra-high net worth clients have been with Citi for more than 10 years.
GWIM consists of two primary businesses: Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank.
Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business provides a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers tailored wealth advisory services to ultra-high-net-worth clients, personalized financial planning, and a full range of private banking services including deposits, loans, and securities execution, with deposits also raised through Marcus.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs describe tailored private banking services aimed at ultra-high-net-worth clients that include deposit alternatives. Citi highlights the scale of its USPB deposit base ($402 billion) and client retention metrics, whereas Goldman Sachs describes the service offerings (loans, deposits, execution) and client acquisition channels (corporate referrals, employee programs) without disclosing specific deposit volumes or retention percentages for this segment.

comparisons.peer_summary: Global Private Bank revenue was $11.4 billion, up 7%, driven by higher noninterest revenue from management fees on strong net inflows and higher average market levels (partially offset by the expiration of First Republic acquired lending-related commitments amortization) and higher net interest income from higher average deposits associated with First Republic, wider spreads on loans, and higher average loans (partially offset by deposit margin compression).
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures concern the Global Private Bank segment and the role of deposits in its financial performance. Citi characterizes its deposit base as strong and diversified with specific retention metrics. JPMorgan provides revenue metrics ($11.4 billion) explicitly driven by net interest income from higher average deposits (including those from First Republic) and noninterest revenue from strong net inflows, indicating similar reliance on deposit growth and asset accumulation within the private banking unit.
